newsitem.title: USA: More New Yorkers find Giuliani likeable - poll.
newsitem.headline: More New Yorkers find Giuliani likeable - poll.

text.p: New Yorkers find Mayor Rudolph Giuliani more "likeable" than they did six months ago, according to a public opinion poll published Tuesday.
The Quinnipiac College Poll found that when asked if the sometimes irascible Giuliani has a likeable personality, respondents were split, 47 percent to 47 percent.
In a a Feb. 11 survey, 52 percent said he does not have a "likeable personality" while 43 percent said they liked him.

The poll by the Hamden, Connecticut, college was conducted July 29 to Aug. 3 and had a margin of error plus or minus 3.6 percent. It surveyed 759 New York City residents who say they are registered voters.

The poll was taken before the national magazine Vanity Fair published a story that alleged Giuliani was having an "intimate" extramarital affair with his communications director, Cristyne Lategano, that had ruined his marriage. Giuliani and Lategano denied the report.
Political pundits and even his possible opponents doubt the report will affect the Giuliani's chances for re-election to a second term this fall.
By a margin of 64 percent to 29 percent, voters approve of Giuliani's work, an increase from 60 percent to 35 percent in a June 18 poll by the independent Quinnipiac College.
Giuliani beats leading Democratic challenger Ruth Messinger by 53 percent to 35 percent, a full 10 percent more than the 49 percent to 39 percent lead he held in the June poll.
